audit_findings.title: The latest debt is paired with a stale interest burden
audit_findings.magnitude: H1 2026 net interest was $29.9m versus $14.5m in H1 2025; annualizing $29.9m implies $59.8m, $18.9m pre-tax or approximately $15.0m after tax above FY2025, equivalent to approximately $5.11-$7.94 per share across the scenarios
audit_findings.mechanism: Equity-level OE retains interest expense, so a higher current interest burden reduces the OE anchor and every projected cash flow rather than entering through a debt deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: Net interest expense of $41 million in 2025 increased slightly from $39 million in 2024 primarily due to increased borrowings as a result of decreased cash flow.
audit_findings.explanation: The mismatch is demonstrated: debt rose to $1,581.3m and H1 2026 net interest more than doubled year over year. However, the computed annualized adjustment is only about 2.0% of the $766.1m anchor. Its estimated per-share effect would not overturn the bear, base, or bull comparison with the $390.53 market price, although it narrows the bull-case margin.
audit_findings.action: Recalculate normalized after-tax interest instrument by instrument using $412.0m of commercial paper at 4.11%, the $300.0m term loan at 4.55%, fixed notes, finance leases, and normalized interest income; rerun only if the resulting OE reduction materially exceeds approximately $15.0m.

audit_findings.title: The null perimeter ruling misses a material late-year acquisition
audit_findings.magnitude: The acquisition contributed $42m of 2025 sales and $6.8m of 2025 segment profit; completed acquisitions contributed $26m of segment profit in H1 2026 ($8m Home Comfort Solutions and $18m Building Climate Solutions); valuation-relevant OE adjustment unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: A pro-forma acquisition perimeter changes normalized OE through acquired operating profit, amortization, maintenance capex, working capital, integration costs and acquisition-related interest; scenario growth could also double count the acquired contribution.
audit_findings.evidence: Subsequent to the purchase of Duro Dyne and Supco, we recognized net sales of approximately $ 42 million and the acquired businesses contributed approximately $ 6.4 million and $ 0.4 million to the Building Climate Solutions and Home Comfort Solutions segment profit, respectively, from the date of acquisition through December 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter omission is demonstrated because the anchor contains only about two months of Duro Dyne and Supco while H1 2026 contains six months and shows a $26m acquisition profit benefit. That contribution is large enough relative to the $766.1m anchor and the narrow bull-case premium to affect the valuation conclusion. Direction remains mixed because omitted operating earnings understate value, while omitted financing, reinvestment or integration burdens overstate it.
audit_findings.action: Prepare a Duro Dyne and Supco pro-forma full-year OE schedule using 2026 sales and segment-profit contribution, cash taxes, incremental interest, amortization, working capital, maintenance capex and integration costs; then rerun all scenarios with acquisition growth removed from organic growth assumptions.

audit_findings.title: Near-term capital spending is far above the anchor-year level
audit_findings.magnitude: The 2026 plan is $250.0m versus $118.8m in 2025, a $131.2m gross increase equal to 17.1% of the $766.1m anchor; H1 2026 spending was $91.2m versus $54.0m in H1 2025; maintenance and compliance portion unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any recurring maintenance or compliance capex omitted from OE reduces distributable cash; capacity and discretionary growth capex instead affects the reinvestment required to achieve forecast growth.
audit_findings.evidence: We expect capital expenditures of approximately $250 million in 2026 for general capital improvement projects .
audit_findings.explanation: The higher spending level is filed and partly realized, but the record identifies H1 spending as strategic land and building investment and does not split the $250m plan between maintenance, compliance and growth. Consequently, the gross difference is potentially material, but the amount that should reduce OE cannot be established.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the 2026 project-level capex budget and classify each project as maintenance, compliance, replacement, capacity or discretionary growth; rerun OE using only recurring maintenance and compliance spending and test growth cases for required capacity investment.

audit_findings.title: A large working-capital cash requirement may be absent from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: The 2025 working-capital increase was $217.0m, equal to 28.3% of the $766.1m anchor; June 2026 inventory was $1,152.4m, essentially unchanged from $1,152.6m at year-end 2025; recurring requirement unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Recurring incremental inventory, receivables and other operating working capital reduce projected OE and the cash distributable to common shareholders.
audit_findings.evidence: The decrease was primarily attributable to an increase in net working capital of $217 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The $217m historical cash requirement is demonstrated, but its normalized valuation effect is unresolved. H1 2026 cash flow improved as the prior-year inventory build did not repeat, yet inventory remained approximately $299m above December 2024, so the record does not establish whether the build will reverse or represents a structural requirement.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the 2025 build and 2026 movements by inventory, receivables, payables, acquisitions and refrigerant-transition stocking; calculate normalized working capital as a percentage of incremental sales and rerun each growth scenario with that cash requirement deducted.

audit_findings.title: The anchor benefits from temporarily reduced compensation and discretionary spending
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 SG&A fell $49.2m to $681.4m; H1 2026 SG&A increased $23.7m to $368.3m, with the filing attributing the increase primarily to higher discretionary and employee-related costs and the acquisition; normalized adjustment unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Restoring recurring incentive compensation and essential discretionary spending reduces normalized OE and sustainable margins used in the growth scenarios.
audit_findings.evidence: As a percentage of net sales, SG&A expenses decreased 60 bps from 13.7% to 13.1% in the same periods, primarily due to lower employee-related costs including reduced incentive compensation and reduced discretionary expenses.
audit_findings.explanation: The temporary cost benefit and its subsequent reversal are both supported by filings. The $49.2m FY2025 SG&A decline and $23.7m H1 2026 increase are large relative to the anchor and could erase the bull case's $16.64 per-share premium over market value if a substantial portion is recurring. Acquisition-related SG&A prevents treating the full increase as normalization without further evidence.
audit_findings.action: Bridge 2024, 2025 and H1 2026 SG&A by cash incentive compensation, headcount, consulting, marketing, acquisition overhead and other discretionary categories; establish scenario-consistent recurring costs and rerun OE and margins without acquisition-related duplication.

audit_findings.title: Long-duration warranty estimates could understate the common-equity burden
audit_findings.mechanism: An under-accrual would overstate historical and projected OE because warranty expense remains an operating cost and is not separately deducted in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Some of the warranties we issue extend 10 years or more in duration and a relatively small adjustment to an assumption may have a significant impact on our overall liability.
audit_findings.explanation: No under-accrual is demonstrated. Warranty expense is already included in cost of goods sold, the liability increased from $167.2m to $174.6m by June 2026, and estimate changes of $2.7m in FY2025 and $3.5m in H1 2026 were recorded. The possible additional burden depends on future failure rates and repair costs, so the present valuation effect cannot be established and should be monitored.
audit_findings.action: Track quarterly claims paid, new-warranty accruals and estimate revisions by product generation, particularly refrigerant-transition products; rerun OE if adverse claim development establishes a recurring charge beyond the recorded accrual.
